title: Restating the Contract Year Out-of-Pocket Total on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Enrollment
content:
The out-of-pocket total restated on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan enrollment for the contract year is what the member has paid on the fills the total is gathered over, less what a supplemental benefit card met at a pharmacy, less what the reversals on the pharmacy record take back out, together with what counts from a fill dispensed by an out-of-network pharmacy. Those amounts are added and subtracted in that order and the total rounded once to two decimal places, and where the total comes out below nothing it is taken as nothing.

## The amounts that enter the total

- The total is gathered over the fills standing paid on the pharmacy record with a fill date in the 3 months up to the handling date.
- Nothing is taken as met by a supplemental benefit card.
- Nothing is taken back out for reversals.
- Nothing counts from a fill dispensed by an out-of-network pharmacy.

## What the restated total then governs

The payment stage the enrollment then shows is read off the restated total rather than kept as a separate fact, so a restatement can return a member to an earlier stage.

## Worked on a hypothetical record

Take a pharmacy record on which the fills standing paid with a fill date in the 3 months up to the handling date carry member payments of 46.00 USD, 12.50 USD and 7.25 USD.

1. What the member has paid on those fills is 65.75 USD.
2. Nothing is taken as met by a supplemental benefit card, so 65.75 USD stands.
3. Nothing is taken back out for reversals, so 65.75 USD stands.
4. Nothing counts from a fill dispensed by an out-of-network pharmacy, so 65.75 USD stands.
5. Rounding that total once to two decimal places leaves 65.75 USD, which is above nothing, so the enrollment is restated at 65.75 USD for the contract year.

Where the same working came out below nothing, the total would be taken as nothing and the enrollment restated at 0.00 USD.
